newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Focus - EU brings GMO soya, maize under food law.
newsitem.headline: Focus - EU brings GMO soya, maize under food law.

text.p: The European Union has decided that genetically modified soya and maize should be brought under the EU novel food law which assesses new foods' safety, a European Commission spokesman said on Friday.

Under the decision, struck by the EU's standing committee for food on Thursday, the European Commission will propose by November 1 a list of products containing GMO soya and maize which it believes should be labelled.

Under the EU's novel foods directive the 15-nation bloc requires labelling of finished foods products only where they are "significantly" different from conventional foods, meaning not all GMO soya and maize will necessarily need to be labelled.
"You have to distinguish between safety evaluation and labelling rules," a Commission official told reporters.
"I do not know whether we will label anything, everthing or something in between, for example those with proteins, but not oil."
The Commission has given itself until November 1 to decide what, if any, products need labelling and what the content of the label should be, the official said.
"You have to allow a bit of time to prepare for this at (European) Community level. We have to decide what goes on the label," he said.
The United States, a massive exporter of GMO maize and soya to Europe, had carefully watched any EU moves to enforce labelling, which it fears could turn sceptical consumers against its produce.

The United States is in particular strongly opposed to any moves to impose the segregation of GMO maize, soybeans and other crops because of the huge cost and because it claims they do not endanger human health.
